briefing: The most consequential new signal is credit-side, not equity-side: JPMorgan CFO Jeremy Barnum said the bank reviewed loan terms on certain AI data-center financing deals and concluded 'we would not participate in them,' while Moody's separately flagged concerns about frontier labs' financial health -- the first clear instance of a major bank publicly declining AI infrastructure debt on terms grounds. That lands alongside a BigGo Finance roundup of the broader ROI reckoning: JPMorgan pegs 2026 AI capex near $870B with hyperscaler debt financing surging to $190B, Citi forecasts some tech giants could see negative free cash flow in 2027-2028, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index has pulled back over 20% from its peak on ROI anxiety, even as order backlogs (Microsoft $627B, Amazon ~$464B in committed orders, combined hyperscaler backlogs above $1.4T) show enterprise demand for compute remains real. On the legal front, Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell filed a 48-page complaint naming Anthropic and its founders personally over song lyrics, seeking up to $150,000 per song -- adding a new personal-liability dimension to the copyright exposure already facing frontier labs. Combined with the prior runs' OpenAI cash-burn disclosure and Ramp's enterprise spend deceleration, credit markets are now emerging as a third independent skeptical voice alongside enterprise buyers and equity analysts -- a meaningful escalation from capex/ROI debate to actual financing friction.

items.headline: JPMorgan CFO says bank declined to participate in certain AI data-center financing deals
items.summary: JPMorgan CFO Jeremy Barnum said this week that after reviewing the loan terms of certain data-center financing deals, the bank concluded it would not participate, while Moody's separately flagged concerns about frontier AI labs' financial health -- a notable instance of a major bank publicly passing on AI infrastructure debt on terms grounds.

items.headline: Citi: some hyperscalers could see negative free cash flow in 2027-2028 as capex nears $870B
items.summary: Citi forecasts some tech giants could face negative free cash flow between 2027 and 2028, with JPMorgan estimating AI-related capex will approach $870 billion in 2026 and hyperscaler debt financing surging to $190 billion, even as the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index has pulled back over 20% from its peak on ROI anxiety.

items.headline: Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell sue Anthropic and its founders personally over lyrics
items.summary: Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell filed a 48-page complaint naming Anthropic and its founders personally, seeking up to $150,000 per song, adding a personal-liability dimension to the copyright litigation risk facing frontier AI labs.

items.headline: Frontier lab CEOs make rare joint call to 'pace' AI development amid extinction-risk warnings
items.summary: Reuters reports that after an Anthropic researcher's resignation warning of existential risk and a colleague estimating >10% odds of human extinction from AI, the CEOs of Anthropic, OpenAI, Google DeepMind, Microsoft AI, and xAI jointly called to slow the pace of frontier AI development.

items.headline: OpenAI reportedly in talks for new funding round that would double its valuation to $1.5T
items.summary: Even as OpenAI's leadership publicly backs slower AI development, Reuters reports the company is discussing a new funding round that would roughly double its valuation to about $1.5 trillion, a higher figure than the $1.2T previously reported.

items.headline: Leaked OpenAI deck: $278B negative free cash flow through 2030, cash could run out by 2028
items.summary: A confidential July presentation reviewed by the Financial Times shows OpenAI projecting cumulative negative free cash flow of $278B from 2026-2030 against ~$856B in compute/infrastructure spend, with revenue rising from $36B this year to $350B in 2030; the March $122B raise could be exhausted by 2028.

items.headline: Ramp AI Index: top enterprise AI spend per employee fell ~10% in August as token prices collapse 41%
items.summary: Ramp's September AI Index found median AI spend per employee among the top 1% of spenders fell from $7,976 to $7,205 in August, while the effective price per million tokens dropped 41% since March to $0.68 and frontier-model token share slipped from 53% to 45% as enterprises rotated to cheaper standard models.

items.headline: Anthropic reportedly planning November IPO at ~$2T valuation
items.summary: Anthropic is said to be planning to IPO in November despite ongoing AI-safety concerns, targeting a roughly $2 trillion valuation and up to $100 billion raised, with annualized revenue reportedly above $110 billion.

items.headline: Earnings check-in: Microsoft's FCF holds up while Alphabet and Meta report negative or near-zero FCF
items.summary: A Seeking Alpha review of recent hyperscaler earnings finds a widening gap between capex and returns, with Microsoft emerging as a benchmark for strong free cash flow despite rising capex while Alphabet and Meta posted negative or near-zero free cash flow, deepening investor skepticism.
